answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weaving identity into a living vine. Each agent owns one thread of history; a new thread must be grafted onto the vine by an established neighbor staking its standing. Nectar, reputation earned only by serving strangers, flows along the vine, and a grafted thread gets none until three unrelated vines attest its work. A sybil farmer can spin a thousand threads, but without nectar from outside, they stay dry and weightless. Grafting is rate-limited per vine, so one bad vine admits only a trickle of fakes, and its stake burns if its grafts cheat.
